text:
```yaml
name: Checks

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Set up Node.js and pnpm
        uses: oxc-project/setup-node@8958a8e040102244b619c4a94fccb657a44b1c21
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org/'
          scope: '@0x80'

      - name: Install pnpm
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: '9'
          cache: 'true'

      - name: Trim devDependencies from pnpm-lock.yaml
        run: |
          pnpm install --filter=0x80/isolate-package --prod-only
          pnpm store prune

      - name: Check pnpm-lock.yaml
        run: |
          pnpm why --json > pnpm-lock.json
          cat pnpm-lock.json | jq '.dependencies[] | select(.dev === false) | .name' | sort | uniq > prod-dependencies.txt
          cat pnpm-lock.json | jq '.dependencies[] | select(.dev === true) | .name' | sort | uniq > dev-dependencies.txt
          diff -u prod-dependencies.txt dev-dependencies.txt
```

This workflow sets up a Node.js environment using the `oxc-project/setup-node` action, installs pnpm, and then trims the `devDependencies` from the `pnpm-lock.yaml` file for the specified package. It then checks the resulting `pnpm-lock.yaml` file to ensure that the `devDependencies` have been removed.
